Index: docs/kit/02-api-reference.md

--- docs/kit/02-api-reference.md
+++ docs/kit/02-api-reference.md
@@ -146,7 +146,7 @@
 
 Online learning now checks HTTP success and versioned, count-conserving application receipts, including the ring-to-statistics credit cascade. Statistics `processed` counts existing accumulator calls whose save was acknowledged; `skipped` counts rows the existing handler did not process. Alarm scheduling is reported separately and does not prove lift publication. A failed mutation/save invalidates cached state; missing, failed or malformed acknowledgements mean unknown or not-attempted work, never a safe automatic retry. Ring receipts keep attributed credits separate from weighted eligible credits and downstream processing; append acceptance is separate from cutoff suppression and the resulting bounded ring/index depths. Current background decision/outcome callers emit one fixed numeric incomplete summary without identifiers, payloads or raw errors. Downstream waits do not hold the ring's read lock or delay the shopper response. This is handler acknowledgement, not unique-event accounting, durable reconciliation/recovery, an atomic erasure fence or publication/completeness assurance; non-idempotent exposure/credit writes are not retried.
 
-Direct attribution now requires an exact, case-sensitive slot match when an outcome names a nonblank slot, for every reward including featured-product purchases. A named miss receives no credit in another slot. Missing/null/blank slots and the SDK's literal `unknown` retain broad legacy matching; `match:any` remains intentionally broad. The shared rule applies to online credits, hourly reconstruction and raw-record reports without changing scope, windows or first/last selection. A real slot named `unknown` remains ambiguous. This does not add correlated decision/page/brand/position identity, change global-item fatigue or served/rendered/viewable units, or provide SDK/dedup acceptance. Existing counters, snapshots and stored reports are not repaired; new recomputation can differ under the unchanged policy label.
+Direct attribution now requires an exact, case-sensitive slot match when an outcome names a nonblank slot, for every reward including featured-product purchases. A named miss receives no credit in another slot. Missing/null/blank slots and the SDK's literal `unknown` retain broad legacy matching; `match:any` remains intentionally broad. The shared rule applies to online credits, hourly reconstruction and raw-record reports without changing scope, windows or first/last selection. A real slot named `unknown` remains ambiguous. The named-slot guard alone does not add correlated decision/page/brand/position identity, change global-item fatigue or served/rendered/viewable units, or provide SDK/dedup acceptance; see the optional exact decision selector in [the integration guide](01-integration-guide.md). Existing counters, snapshots and stored reports are not repaired; new recomputation can differ under the unchanged policy label.
 
 Learning ingestion has conservative application budgets independent of gamma:256KiB/1000 rows per statistics request;256-code-unit scope/item/cell components and2048-byte keys;512KiB,256 items and4096 total item-plus-slot counters per stored value. An over-cap batch is refused whole with413 and `applied:false`, before any counter save; no eviction, coarsening, remapping or retry is performed. Existing ineligible rows still count as skipped. Malformed/oversized existing state and owner mismatch return503 requiring recovery, without automatic reset. Save/reset acknowledgement failure invalidates cache; a reset-item publication failure after deletion returns503 without claiming rollback. The existing explicit reset remains available.
 
@@ -166,6 +166,8 @@
 
 Decision-ring append/outcome requests are bounded at1MiB of actual UTF-8 JSON, with1000 append records and2048-byte decision/outcome/index IDs. The full stored ring-plus-index candidate is limited to1MiB and4096 index entries, preserving the existing200-record/7-day ring and90-day index age rules without new eviction or projection. Capacity overflow refuses the whole ring append before saving with413 and `applied:false`; this is ring-local, not rollback of concurrently accepted statistics exposures. Existing fan-out reports incomplete without retry. Malformed/oversized saved state returns503 without history or credits; explicit reset remains reachable and ambiguous save/reset acknowledgements force reload. Full decision records remain available, but rich payloads can reach the byte cap before200 records. These are synthetic-tested application budgets, not native-limit, sustained-capacity, complete-history or recovery guarantees.
 
+Upgraded ring append receipts use `version:2`, conserving `received = accepted + duplicates + cutoffSkipped`. After fresh subject/erasure checks, exact repeats of a unique retained full record or an earlier input add no ring/index row, before state-cap admission. Every JSON field participates: object key order is irrelevant, array order and values are exact. `accepted` counts new unique inputs before existing age/depth retention, not resulting depth or statistics processing. Changed same-ID payloads, ambiguous retained full-record IDs and index-only collisions refuse the entire append with409, fixed `ring decision collision` and `applied:false`. Unrelated historical duplicates are not repaired. A full record without an index entry still proves a repeat; an index alone cannot. Deduplication is limited to retained evidence, with no guarantee after existing pruning/reset removes it. Current fan-out validates/surfaces v2 and reads v1 as legacy acceptance without invented duplicate counts. Older v1-only callers see v2 as an unknown acknowledgement and must not retry. Repeated full fan-out still repeats independent statistics exposure/credit writes: this is ring-only containment, not a new exposure unit, history repair, durable reconciliation or exactly-once pipeline.
+
 New learning updates keep each counter at its latest event timestamp and discount late contributions to that reference, without re-aging existing evidence. Snapshot counts, rates and lifts retain JavaScript numeric precision through serialization, evidence thresholds and raw decision explanations; human-readable sentences may round for presentation. Shrinkage, prior strength, clamps, true-zero-reference fallback and gamma-zero behavior are unchanged. Repeated inputs still add; this is not idempotency. Damaged historical counters, old rounded snapshots/reports and supplied replay snapshots are not repaired or reset. Lateness/future-time policy, generations and trustworthy reconstruction remain separate work. More precise numeric JSON can reach existing byte budgets earlier.
